title: 군대 왔어요?
scene: 소개팅으로 처음 만난 카페. A 는 연습해 온 「-습니다」 인사를 한다
goal: Switching from formal speech to 반말 on a first date

turns.speaker: B
turns.en: You're {name}, right? You look exactly like your photo!

turns.speaker: A
turns.en: Good day. It's a pleasure to meet you. I'm {name}.
turns.note: -습니다 = very formal — interviews, the army, news

turns.speaker: B
turns.ko: ㅋㅋㅋㅋ 뭐야, 군대 말투야? 훈련소 다녀왔어요?
turns.rd: ㅋㅋㅋㅋ mwoya, gundae maltuya? hullyeonso danyeowasseoyo?
turns.en: Hahaha what, army talk? Did you just get out of boot camp?
turns.note: Kick: 군대 말투 = army talk · 훈련소 = boot camp — -습니다 sounds like a soldier

turns.speaker: A
turns.en: Uh… is it weird? That's how I learned it from the book.

turns.speaker: B
turns.ko: 아니, 귀여워서 그래. 우리 말 놓을까?
turns.rd: ani, gwiyeowoseo geurae. uri mal noeulkka?
turns.en: No, it's just cute. Shall we drop the formalities?
turns.note: 말 놓을까? = shall we speak casually (반말)?

turns.speaker: B
turns.en: Drop the “-ssi” too. Just call me Yujin.
turns.note: 씨 = polite name suffix — friends drop it

turns.speaker: A
turns.en: Yujin-a…? Ugh, whatever, this is too hard!
turns.note: 유진아 = name + 아 (friends' way to call) · 아 몰라 = ugh, whatever

review.final: 2026-11-02 Grok 2회차 재작성본 그대로 + 검사기용 최소 수정
